entries.title: I Chronicles 27:1
segments:
Twenty and four thousand; these were kept constantly under military discipline, and were changed for as many others once a month. 
 
In those services which are needful for the public safety, all should be willing to take part; and as far as consistent, these services should be so divided as to bear equally upon all according to their ability.

entries.title: I Chronicles 27:3
segments: Of the children of Perez was the chief; or, Of the children ofPerez was he, being chief, etc.  Perez is, in the Hebrew, the same as Pharez the son of Judah, from whom also David descended.

entries.title: I Chronicles 27:4
segments: The ruler; a subordinate ruler under Dodai.

entries.title: I Chronicles 27:7
segments: Asahel--Zebadiah his son after him; Asahel had been slain at the beginning of David's reign, but his son Zebadiah seems to have succeeded him in the command of his division, which retained the name of Asahel's division.  When David--how early in his reign we are not informed--divided the army into the twelve divisions here mentioned, Asahel's came in as the fourth.

entries.title: I Chronicles 27:23
segments:
From twenty years old and under; these being unfit for military service, and exceedingly numerous, he did not attempt the labor of numbering them. 
 
It may sometimes be expedient and useful for the people of a country to be numbered; but this should be done for useful purposes and not to gratify pride, or lead men to glory in their numbers, prosperity or strength.

entries.title: I Chronicles 27:24
segments: Began to number; that is, to number the men of war who were twenty years old and upward.

entries.title: I Chronicles 27:25
segments: The division of labor, and the appointment of suitable persons to superintend every department of business, are essential to that regularity, diligence, and dispatch, which the highest prosperity and usefulness indispensibly require.
